module_microarchitecture.name: active_aero_controller_cfg
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Synchronous register/control block with simple address decode, readback muxing, and latched configuration storage.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: On each clock, honor readable/writable config accesses, update only the defined configuration fields, and present stable latched outputs to the engine. Treat the reference-condition record as ordinary configuration state that is reset to the specified defaults.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Use a small set of synchronous configuration registers plus readback/output registers. No complex FSM is required; reset returns all stored configuration to safe non-actuating defaults and restores the reference-condition record.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive cfg_rdata and cfg_ready from the register interface, and continuously drive the semantic configuration outputs for model ID, checkpoint ID, timeout/freshness thresholds, actuator bounds, rate limit, fallback command, supported geometry format, control_gain, intent map selector, and reference-condition metadata.
ownership_notes: Owns only the configuration register state and readback behavior.
Does not own request sequencing, response checking, or actuator control.
Must not drive any external response inputs or actuator outputs.

module_microarchitecture.name: active_aero_controller_engine
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Single-clock protocol and safety datapath using counters, comparators, muxes, saturating arithmetic, and simple request/outstanding tracking.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Combine input qualification, envelope and format checks, outstanding-request gating, response validation, and safety arbitration in a straight-through synchronous datapath. A request is issued only when inputs are qualified and no request is outstanding. A response is accepted only when the sequence matches, freshness is within threshold, and all required fields are present. Any violation selects deterministic fallback.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Maintain a one-deep outstanding-request tracker, an incrementing sequence counter, a local request time/cycle tag, validation/fault flags, previous-command storage for rate limiting, and saturating diagnostic counters. Keep the state machine intentionally minimal: idle/no-outstanding versus outstanding/ սպաս pending, with synchronous fault/fallback latching as needed.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: When a validated response exists, form a placeholder model-driven intent via the programmable control_gain or intent_map_sel path, then clamp and optionally rate-limit each actuator command field. When validation fails or any fault is present, drive the configured safe fallback command after the same clamp/rate-limit stage. Assert actuator_cmd_valid whenever a command vector is produced, including fallback if that is the selected safe policy. Expose fault_status bits and all diagnostic counters synchronously.
ownership_notes: Owns request packing, outstanding sequence tracking, response checking, safety arbitration, clamp/rate limiting, fallback selection, fault encoding, and diagnostics.
Does not own configuration storage or the external model service.
Must never allow stale, mismatched, unsupported, or invalid response data to influence actuator command output.

sequencing_notes: Configuration is latched in the cfg block and then consumed as stable control constants by the engine.
The engine should issue at most one outstanding request at a time; additional request opportunities are blocked until the current request is resolved or timed out.
The request sequence counter increments only on accepted request issuance and is embedded in model_req_payload.
model_rsp_valid is only acted upon when an outstanding request exists and the response sequence matches the outstanding sequence.
Response freshness is checked against the configured threshold using the response timestamp or local age/cycle tag before any model fields are used.

If geometry_valid and flow_valid are asserted, geometry format matches the configured supported format, and flow_velocity_mps is within 20..55 m/s inclusive, request issuance may proceed when the engine is otherwise idle and not fault-latched into fallback.
Any envelope violation, unsupported format, stale/mismatched response, or invalid required field drives safe fallback behavior and blocks stale command propagation.
Validated response data is never used directly as physics; it is only a digital placeholder input to the programmable intent mapping path before clamp/rate limiting.
timing_notes: All sequential behavior is synchronous to clk with active-low synchronous reset rst_n.
Reset must clear request tracking, sequence state, validation flags, fault latches, previous command history, actuator outputs, and saturating counters to safe defaults.
Configuration outputs and engine control outputs should be updated on the clock edge; combinational comparators and muxing may be used within the cycle for qualification and arbitration.
Clamping and rate limiting are intended as simple combinational or single-cycle registered stages, not multi-cycle pipelines unless later required by implementation details.
Diagnostic counters saturate at all-ones and must not wrap.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
